stemBlocks.value: W = (3  6 / -2  5). (a)(i) Find the 2x2 matrix L such that W + L is the zero matrix. (ii) Find the 2x2 matrix P such that WP is the identity matrix. (b) A right-angled triangle M has vertices X(1, 1), Y(3, 1) and Z(3, 4). M is transformed by the matrix N = (0  1 / 1  0) to give the image M'. Find the coordinates of the vertices of M'.
Think first: L is the additive inverse of W and P is the multiplicative inverse of W, so one part needs sign changes and the other needs a determinant.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p291-q02 from workbook page 291.

solutionSteps.instruction: For L, change the sign of every element of W so that each pair adds to zero.
For P, note that WP = I means P is the inverse of W, so first find det W.
Swap the leading diagonal entries, change the sign of the other two, and divide by the determinant.
For (b), write each vertex as a column matrix and multiply on the left by N.

contentBlocks.value: N = (0  1 / 1  0) swaps the two coordinates, which is a reflection in the line y = x.

strategyBlocks.value: Write L as the negative of W, compute the inverse of W for P using the determinant and adjugate, then multiply N by each vertex written as a column matrix.

whyThisWorks.value: Adding matrices works entry by entry, so the matrix that cancels W must be the one whose entries are the negatives of W's. Multiplication is different: WP = I says P undoes W, and for a 2x2 matrix that inverse is the adjugate divided by the determinant. Transforming a point means multiplying its position vector, written as a column, by the transformation matrix, which is why the image coordinates come out one vertex at a time.

commonErrors.misconception: Confusing the additive inverse with the multiplicative inverse and giving L as the inverse of W.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Confusing the additive inverse with the multiplicative inverse and giving L as the inverse of W.

commonErrors.misconception: Dividing by the wrong determinant, for example 15 - 12 = 3 instead of 15 + 12 = 27.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Dividing by the wrong determinant, for example 15 - 12 = 3 instead of 15 + 12 = 27.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing the vertices as row matrices and multiplying in the wrong order.

Avoid this: Leaving P without the factor 1/27.

examTip.value: Check any inverse you find by multiplying it back by the original matrix; you should get (1  0 / 0  1) exactly.
